case.pattern_description: A coordinated multi-card fraud scheme characterized by bursts of two or more online purchases for Product C valued between $510 and $963, conducted through anonymous proxies (IP_PROXY:ANONYMOUS). Rather than sharing a single device fingerprint, the perpetrators rotate to a distinct newly generated device profile for each transaction to evade device-fingerprinting and ring-detection controls. The activity emerged abruptly across multiple distinct cardholders and customers in January 2017 with no historical precedent in prior months.

case.summary: Following an analyst review request, card C06220-K1 was investigated for an anomalous burst of three online Product C purchases totaling $2,166.71 between January 17 and January 19, 2017 (transactions 3660125, 3660126, and 3660127). These transactions sharply deviated from established cardholder history and were conducted through anonymous proxies using rotating, newly generated device profiles (D009715, D009718, and D009721) to evade device-fingerprint detection. Cross-card analysis revealed an identical coordinated fraud scheme emerging simultaneously across three peer cards belonging to unrelated customers (C05061-K1, C07925-K1, and C10553-K1) during January 2017. Card C06220-K1 also has five prior confirmed fraud cases in its record. The activity was confirmed as an undocumented coordinated multi-card fraud scheme, resulting in card blocking, connected card monitoring, and regulatory reporting.

sar.narrative: This Suspicious Activity Report details an undocumented card-not-present fraud scheme impacting customer C06220 and card C06220-K1, totaling $2,166.71 across three transactions. Between January 17, 2017, and January 19, 2017, card C06220-K1 was used online for three high-value purchases of Product C: transaction 3660125 ($637.13, region 330), transaction 3660126 ($758.80, region 384), and transaction 3660127 ($770.78, region 126). Prior to this burst, card C06220-K1 had zero online Product C transactions across 69 baseline transactions, representing an acute deviation from normal cardholder behavior. All three transactions were conducted through an anonymous proxy service (IP_PROXY:ANONYMOUS) using a rotating newly generated device profile for each separate charge: device D009715, device D009718, and device D009721. This systematic rotation of new devices behind anonymous proxies indicates a deliberate evasion technique to circumvent device-fingerprinting and linked-ring detection rules. Graph analytics identified the identical signature emerging simultaneously across three peer cards belonging to unrelated customers in January 2017: C05061-K1 (customer C05061), C07925-K1 (customer C07925), and C10553-K1 (customer C10553), with zero occurrences in the preceding two months. The peer transactions (3660101, 3660103, 3660106, 3660107, 3660111, and 3660112) demonstrate coordinated abuse across multiple accounts. Card C06220-K1 has also been subject to five prior confirmed fraud cases (CC-0626, CC-2539, CC-2807, CC-4224, and CC-5379). Consequently, card C06220-K1 has been blocked, connected peer cards have been routed for monitoring, and this filing documents the coordinated compromise.

stop_reason: The investigation stopped pursuant to Policy Section 6 because the fraud probability reached 0.955, exceeding the 0.85 decisive threshold, supported by multiple independent evidentiary signals across cardholder behavior, device evasion techniques, cross-card links, and prior fraud history, such that further inquiries would not alter the decision.
